title: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings raises $2B to bring AI to the enterprise
slides: It targets slow enterprise AI adoption
Most Fortune 500 pilots never leave sandbox
You can now get AI without building it
Test one legacy workflow before competitors do
thread_text:
1. Why $2B now?

Thrive just raised $2B because enterprises are stuck in pilot purgatory—most Fortune 500 AI tests never leave the sandbox.

2. The sandbox trap

Companies run endless pilots that fail to scale. The real bottleneck isn't tech—it's the slow crawl from proof to production.

3. AI without building

Now you can buy AI as a service—no in-house team needed. This shifts the power from builders to buyers who can deploy fast.

4. The urgency

Competitors are already testing one legacy workflow. If you wait, they'll own the learning curve and the efficiency edge.

5. Your move

Does your company have a pilot stuck in the sandbox? Test one legacy workflow this week—before your rivals do.

instagram.caption:
$2 billion just went to a company whose entire pitch is “stop running AI pilots that never ship.”  

Most Fortune 500 tests die in the sandbox—proof of concept, then nothing. Thrive’s bet is that you’ll buy AI as a service instead of building it in-house. ⏱️  

The bottleneck was never the tech, it was the crawl from pilot to production. Now the buyer beats the builder.  

For you: the fastest path to using this is not starting a new project, but picking one legacy workflow and forcing it to go live this quarter.  

Which one of your workflows is still stuck in a demo? 🧪
